_about: Short implementation notes and typical evidence per CyFun 2025 BASIC requirement. Written for this tool as a working summary; the authoritative text is the CCB booklet 'CyberFundamentals 2025, BASIC' (version 2025-10-01) on https://www.cyfun.eu. Guidance items use 'should' and are not requirements.

guidance: Keep a list of the laws, regulations and contracts that impose information or cybersecurity obligations on the organisation (NIS2, GDPR, sector rules, customer contracts, insurance terms).
Name an owner and a review trigger (at least yearly and when the business changes).
Trace each obligation to the policy, procedure or control that implements it.
evidence: Compliance register or obligations list with owner and review date
References from policies to the obligations they implement
Minutes or a record of the last review

guidance: Write a short information and cybersecurity risk management strategy: risk appetite, how risks are assessed (criteria for probability and impact), how they are treated and who decides.
Treat cybersecurity risks together with other business risks and allocate budget and people to protect business-critical assets.
Update the strategy when the organisation, its systems or the threat landscape change.
evidence: Approved risk management strategy or policy with risk criteria
Risk register with treatment decisions
Management review record showing cybersecurity risk on the agenda

guidance: Identify who has access to the most critical information and technology and make sure that access is authenticated, preferably with MFA.
Cover the whole HR cycle: recruitment, onboarding, role changes and offboarding, including removal of access.
Consider background checks for sensitive roles, within the limits of the law.
evidence: List of critical systems with named authorised users
Onboarding and offboarding checklist including account provisioning and removal
MFA registration report for privileged users

guidance: Have an approved information security policy and the procedures that support it; keep them short and practical.
Communicate the policy at onboarding and after every significant change; keep it easy to find.
Review at least yearly and after organisational or technological change; record approval and review dates.
Include the risk assessment criteria (probability, impact) in the policy set.
evidence: Policy document with version, approver and date
Document register with review dates
Proof of communication (onboarding record, intranet page, acknowledgement)

guidance: Keep an inventory of physical and virtual infrastructure: servers, workstations, network devices, storage, cloud environments and hosting accounts.
Record type, location or provider, owner, configuration or model and lifecycle status.
Use automated discovery where available (device management, cloud provider APIs) and review after deployments, decommissions and moves.
evidence: Asset inventory export (this tool: Assets, kinds hardware, network, cloud)
Connector snapshot of managed devices or cloud resources
Record of the last inventory review

guidance: Keep an inventory of software, SaaS services, APIs and business systems with version, owner, purpose, licence and environment.
Automate discovery where possible (tenant application lists, code repositories, hosting platforms).
Link software and services to the infrastructure they run on.
evidence: Software and service inventory (this tool: Assets, kinds software, service)
Connector snapshot of repositories, hosted services and enterprise applications
Record of the last inventory review

guidance: Classify assets as primary (directly support core business) or secondary (support or protect primary assets) and document the definitions.
Assess criticality on operational, financial, legal, safety and reputational impact; use one consistent scoring method.
Assign an owner to every asset and review priorities at least yearly or after major change.
evidence: Asset register with classification, criticality and owner
Documented criticality criteria and primary/secondary definitions
Record of the yearly review

guidance: Identify the data the organisation stores and processes, regardless of format or location.
Classify it (for example Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) and map it to the systems and services that hold it.
Keep the data inventory updated together with the hardware and software inventories.
evidence: Data inventory with classification and storage location (this tool: Assets, kind data)
Data classification scheme
Mapping of data types to systems

guidance: Install patches and security updates for operating systems and critical components as soon as possible; enable automatic updates on trusted networks.
Use central patch management where available and keep only supported, vendor-maintained software; decommission end-of-life software.
Where automation is not possible, follow a fixed schedule (for example monthly) and keep a rollback procedure.
Download updates from trusted sources only.
evidence: Patch or update policy and schedule
Device compliance or update status report from the management platform
Dependency vulnerability alerts and their resolution for in-house software
List of unsupported software with decommissioning decisions

guidance: List the relevant assets (software, networks, systems, facilities) and the threats and vulnerabilities that apply to them.
Act on vulnerabilities reported by vendors, service providers and government advisories; active scanning is not required at BASIC.
Keep a simple risk register and review it when systems are added or the threat landscape changes.
evidence: Risk register (this tool: Risk register)
Subscription to vendor or CCB advisories and examples of follow-up
Open vulnerability alerts and their treatment

guidance: Perform and document a risk assessment that combines threats, vulnerabilities and business impact for critical processes and assets.
Include human factors and, where relevant, operational technology.
Review and update the assessment regularly and after significant change.
evidence: Assurance level risk assessment (this tool: Risk assessment) with rationale
Risk register with likelihood, impact and treatment
Record of review dates

guidance: After every incident, hold a structured review: what happened, why, how the response went, what to change.
Document lessons learned and share them with the people involved.
Update policies, procedures and tooling from the findings; review the policy set at least yearly.
evidence: Post-incident review template and completed reviews
Change log of procedures showing updates driven by lessons learned
Incident log

guidance: Request, approve and document access formally; use individual accounts, no shared passwords.
Change default passwords before activation, disable unused accounts immediately and limit administrator accounts.
Enforce a password policy and assign rights through groups or roles.
Give devices a unique identifier and label them; secure remote access with encrypted protocols and MFA.
evidence: Access management procedure and password policy
User and account inventory from the identity provider (connector snapshot)
Access request and approval records
Stale or disabled account report

guidance: Change default administrative credentials of wireless access points, use WPA2 or WPA3 with AES and keep firmware updated.
Isolate guest Wi-Fi from internal systems (separate SSID or VLAN) and restrict it; disable it when not needed.
Restrict physical access to access points and monitor for rogue access points.
evidence: Wireless configuration export or screenshots (encryption, guest isolation)
Access point inventory with firmware version
Network diagram showing guest separation

guidance: Require MFA for all remote access: email, VPN, remote desktop, cloud services and web portals, including third parties.
Prefer phishing-resistant methods (FIDO2, passkeys); avoid SMS and e-mail codes.
Combine MFA with strong passwords, up-to-date anti-malware and phishing awareness.
evidence: Conditional Access policy or security defaults requiring MFA (connector check)
MFA registration report showing coverage of all users
VPN or remote access configuration showing MFA

guidance: Define access permissions per system and review the lists periodically and at role changes or departures; revoke unnecessary rights at once.
Give every user and contractor a separate account; restrict guest accounts; use single sign-on where appropriate.
Document the permission management procedure.
evidence: Access control procedure
Latest access review with sign-off
Role or group definitions and membership exports

guidance: Determine who needs access to business-critical information and technology and limit access to those people.
Define the means of access (keys, accounts, codes, administrative privileges) and manage and monitor them.
Allow only healthy endpoints (patched, anti-malware active) to reach critical systems.
evidence: List of business-critical systems with authorised users and access method
Device compliance requirement in access policies
Review record of critical access

guidance: Apply least privilege: start with low privileges, elevate only when justified and for a limited time.
Keep an inventory of accounts and their permissions; use separate accounts for contractors.
Use role-based access control where feasible and harden systems (disable unused ports, services and legacy protocols).
evidence: Account and permission inventory
Role definitions with assigned permissions
Hardening baseline or configuration export

guidance: Separate administrative accounts from daily-use accounts; nobody works, browses or reads mail with administrative privileges.
Use unique local administrator passwords per system and disable unused accounts.
Limit the number of global or domain administrators and review them regularly.
evidence: List of privileged accounts and their owners (connector check: global administrators)
Policy statement on separate admin accounts
Local administrator password management (for example LAPS) configuration

guidance: Manage keys, badges and alarm codes; collect them at departure and change codes regularly.
Give external providers time-limited, logged access only when needed.
Protect critical zones (server room, network cabinets) with locks, alarms or cameras; do not expose network ports in public areas.
evidence: Physical access procedure and badge or key register
Visitor or contractor access log
Photos or description of server room and cabinet protection

guidance: Run an awareness programme for all personnel, contractors and partners: at onboarding and at least yearly, with reminders in between.
Cover phishing, passwords, social engineering, safe remote work and the consequences of policy violations.
Align content with the organisation's policies and keep it current with new threats and incident lessons.
evidence: Awareness programme description and yearly plan
Attendance or completion records
Training material or phishing simulation results

guidance: Wipe data from computers, phones, drives and media before reuse, repair, disposal or return; shred paper.
Enable remote wipe on laptops and mobile devices.
Manage domain names: auto-renew, update references and remove accounts tied to old domains.
evidence: Disposal procedure and disposal records or certificates
Mobile device management configuration showing remote wipe
Domain inventory with renewal settings

guidance: Back up business-critical data and system configurations on a system separate from the source: another device, network segment or location.
Keep at least one copy offline or otherwise isolated from the production network (ransomware protection).
Define recovery objectives (RTO, RPO), test restores and document the backup schedule.
evidence: Backup policy with scope, schedule, retention and storage location
Backup job reports and the latest restore test record
Description of the isolated or offline copy

guidance: Enable logging on operating systems, applications, cloud services and security tools; include audit, security, system and application logs.
Protect logs against unauthorised access, back them up and define retention periods.
Review logs for anomalies and keep a record of the reviews.
evidence: Logging and monitoring procedure with retention periods
Evidence that audit logging is active in the tenant, hosting platform and edge services (connector checks)
Log review records

guidance: Use web filtering (URL, DNS or content filtering) to block malicious and inappropriate sites.
Configure e-mail filtering against spam, phishing and malicious attachments or links.
Keep filter rules and threat feeds updated and align them with the security policy.
evidence: E-mail protection policy configuration (anti-phishing, anti-malware, safe links)
DNS or web filtering policy (connector check: gateway rules)
Filter effectiveness report

guidance: Place a firewall between the internal network and the internet; configure it deny-all-by-default with documented exceptions.
Run and update a software firewall on all endpoints, also when on VPN or remote.
Secure home and remote routers (firewall on, default credentials changed, updates applied); consider intrusion detection.
evidence: Firewall rule base export or review record
Network diagram with firewall placement
Endpoint firewall policy from the device management platform
Web application firewall settings for internet-facing services (connector check)

guidance: Split the network into zones (office, servers, guest, production, management) and control traffic between zones with firewall rules.
Align zones with trust and asset criticality; allow only necessary communication; avoid flat networks.
Separate IT and OT networks where OT exists; treat VLANs as one layer of a defence in depth, not as the only control.
evidence: Network diagram with zones and trust boundaries
Inter-zone firewall rules
Segmentation design decision record

guidance: Run host-based firewalls on all endpoints and servers to detect and block suspicious traffic at the device.
Group systems by function or criticality; put public-facing services in a DMZ.
Limit the number of internet gateways and define inbound and outbound rules.
evidence: Endpoint firewall status report
Network design showing DMZ and gateways
Firewall rule documentation

guidance: Install anti-malware on all devices: desktops, laptops, servers, smartphones and tablets; update at least daily and run scheduled scans.
Apply the same protection to home computers and personal devices used for work.
Manage configurations and alerts centrally and feed alerts into incident response.
evidence: Anti-malware deployment and status report from the management console
Device compliance policy requiring anti-malware (connector check)
Alert handling procedure

guidance: Use endpoint and network protection tools that detect dangerous user behaviour: EDR, intrusion detection or prevention, web application firewall, identity threat detection.
Combine tools so that device, network and identity activity are visible.
Make sure alerts reach someone who acts on them.
evidence: EDR or endpoint protection configuration and coverage report
WAF or intrusion detection configuration (connector check)
Alert routing and response records

guidance: Enable logging on protection and detection tools (firewall, anti-malware, EDR, intrusion detection).
Back up and retain the logs for a defined period based on legal and operational needs.
Review logs and dashboards on a schedule, configure automated alerts and define follow-up actions for repeated patterns.
evidence: Log retention settings and backup evidence for security tools
Scheduled log review procedure and completed review records
Alert configuration screenshots

guidance: Write an incident response plan with detection, containment, communication and recovery steps for critical systems.
Define roles, responsibilities and authorities, with contact details, who starts recovery and who talks to regulators, partners and media.
Review the plan after incidents and changes; test it with tabletop exercises.
evidence: Approved incident response plan with contact list
Incident log and completed incident reports
Tabletop exercise record

guidance: Include a communication protocol in the incident response plan: channels, who informs whom, and prepared message templates.
Write messages in plain language stating what happened, what is affected and what employees must do.
Give management a high-level summary of impact, risk and actions.
evidence: Communication section of the incident response plan
Message templates for employees and management
Examples of communications sent during incidents or exercises

guidance: Document a recovery process for disasters and cybersecurity incidents: who may start recovery, immediate protective actions, backup sites and contact lists.
Align it with the incident response plan and the backup strategy.
Make sure the people with recovery responsibilities know the plan and their authorisations.
evidence: Recovery or continuity plan with roles and contact lists
Restore test results
Awareness or walkthrough record for the recovery team
